Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

bore verb

make someone weary

also be a bore, a bore, you’re boring me, don’t be a bore

classical

Plaut. Cist. 1.1.120: aurēs graviter obtundō tuās (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Att. 8.1: longīs epistulīs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 281

obtundō, obtundere, obtudī, obtūsum

verb, third conjugation, transitive · Conjugation on Wiktionary

weary (by going on), din, bore

Literally “beat against, blunt”: to tire someone by saying a thing too often or too long. “You’re boring me” is obtundis (Ter. And. 348, see understand).

Other words

  • odiōsus, odiōsa, odiōsum — tiresome, a bore

    also used · classical · Traupman 94: nē sīs odiōsus, “don’t be a bore” · Declension on Wiktionary

    Of a person or a thing that gets on one’s nerves; odiōsus esse is “to be a bore”.

  • molestus, molesta, molestum — tiresome, annoying

    also used · classical · Traupman 281: bores molestī · Declension on Wiktionary

    Troublesome, a nuisance; nisi molestum est, “if it’s no trouble”.

Examples

  • aurēs graviter obtundō tuās, nē quem amēs

    I keep dinning it into your ears that you shouldn’t fall in love with anyonePlaut. Cist. 1.1.120 (Lewis & Short)

  • Nōlī mē obtundere!

    Don’t go on at me!composed

See also be bored, understand, tired.
